_note: Keystone seed — architectural PRACTICES (kind=practice). Transferable structural moves, not libraries. A project 'uses' a practice when it has a capability/facet matching one of these. The data-driven domain ontology is the canonical practice-transfer example (built for a multi-tenant platform; data-heavy multi-tenant projects benefit). better_than edges compare a practice to its anti-pattern, task-scoped.

solutions.name: data-driven domain ontology
solutions.description: Entity types, properties, and relationships stored as DATA (rows) rather than hardcoded in application code, so the domain model is configurable per-customer without a redeploy — one platform serves different segments without forking.

solutions.name: hardcoded domain schema
solutions.description: Entity types defined in application code; changing the model means a code change, release, and test cycle.

solutions.name: event sourcing
solutions.description: Persist state as an append-only log of events; current state is a fold. Gives a full audit trail and temporal queries.

solutions.name: outbox pattern
solutions.description: Write domain changes and their outbound events in one transaction (an 'outbox' table), then relay — exactly-once-ish event publishing without dual-write races.

solutions.name: cqrs
solutions.description: Separate read and write models so each scales and is shaped independently.

solutions.name: pgvector semantic search
solutions.description: Store embeddings in Postgres (pgvector) with IVFFlat/HNSW indexes for semantic retrieval alongside relational data — no separate vector DB.

solutions.name: computed/derived properties
solutions.description: Define derived fields (e.g. 'is_recent') evaluated at query time from base data, rather than denormalizing and maintaining them.

better_than.task: serving multiple customers/segments from one platform without forking
better_than.source: a data-driven domain model is changed by a row, not a release — the multi-tenant-without-forking move
